reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a highly regular, near-square-wave periodic pattern with a robust period of 96 points (1 cycle per 96 samples), consistent across all candidates. Each cycle contains a sharp upward spike (rise time ~1–2 points) to a peak between 2.4 and 3.3 robust-standardized units, followed by an abrupt drop to baseline (0.0) within 1–2 points—forming a narrow, symmetric pulse. Baseline is stable at 0.0 with negligible drift; slope_per_point values near zero confirm absence of trend. Amplitude at the 90th percentile is tightly clustered around 2.41–2.47, indicating low amplitude variability. Peaks are consistently sharp and isolated, with minimal shoulder or rounding; troughs are flat at 0.0 with no undershoot. Noise is extremely low: roughness ≈ 0.0 in three candidates, and only candidate 2 shows mild roughness (0.056), likely due to minor local irregularities rather than systemic noise. Boundary truncation is absent—the pulses align cleanly at window edges, confirming the windows were cut at integer multiples of the period. Minor morphological variations exist: candidate 0 shows slightly broader peaks and a single anomalous high plateau (~2.86) early on; candidates 1–3 show more uniform pulse heights and sharper transitions. Overall, normal behavior is defined by crisp, repeatable unit-width pulses spaced exactly 96 points apart, with amplitude bounded roughly [0, 3.3] and shape invariant across cycles.
